originalTitle: European Athletics Championships: Double gold for Great Britain in 4x100m relays – as it happened
summary: GB’s women and men triumphed in the 4x100 relays, and Andreas Almgren aced the men’s 10,000m for Sweden
content: No sooner had Amy Hunt won a staggering third European gold medal in five days than she pointed at the superwomen guiding her closer to history. “We’re the fantastic four,” she said. It was hard to argue with that, especially after watching Britain’s 4x100m women power to glory in 42.05 secs, more than 10 metres clear of Switzerland and Poland. “It’s such a privilege to be able to step on the track with these ladies, and the individual superpowers that we bring,” said Hunt. “It’s no joke. We’re all superwomen together out there.” Sean Ingle’s report from Birmingham will be coming up shortly. A third consecutive European title for Yaroslava Mahuchikh of Ukraine. Poland’s Maria Zodzik wins silver, Montenegro’s Marija Vukovic bronze. Andy Diaz of Italy, meanwhile, took the men’s triple jump, with an effort of 18.15m. Pedro Pichardo of Portugal takes silver with 17.76m, Italy’s Andrea Dallavalle’s claims bronze with 17.37m. Via the BBC, from analyst Jessica Ennis Hill, on those 4x100 relay victories for Great Britain: “A really unique moment, as we often have a situation where one relay team does well and the other drops a baton. To have them both together celebrating is a unique moment for them. Two fantastic gold medals.” Italy (eight gold, four silver, five bronze) 17 Great Britain (six gold, five silver, one bronze) 12 Germany (four gold, seven silver, four bronze) 15 Netherlands (four gold, three silver, five bronze) 12 Norway (four gold, 0 silver, two bronze) 6 A family photo for the Great Britain men’s and women’s relay teams. Great success! “My job is just to put these ladies in a great position so they can show off their excellence and their talents,” says Asher-Smith. “I was just thinking, just run as fast as you can! And let’s get that baton home first.” “I am stood next to the real-lift GOAT,” Hunt says of Asher-Smith. “She’s the most decorated European athlete in history. “She’s got thousands of medals … I am stood next to some amazing women … that was stunning to come together. It’s the time of my life.” “We came here to win, to be honest, to get the gold,” says Eduan. “We knew what we came here to do. The crowd was amazing.” “I had the time of my life,” says Imani Lansiquot. “These girls are so phenomenal, I know I say it all the time … they put me in the best possible position where I could just be free and enjoy it,” says Imani Lansiquot. “I’m so, so happy, and that will be a memory for life.” That’s a dominant win for GB! Superb third and fourth changeovers in particular … And that is Amy Hunt’s third gold of the week. Dina Asher-Smith, Imani-Lara Lansiquot, Success Eduan, and Hunt absolutely fantastic. Switzerland win silver, Poland bronze – Italy in fourth, out of the medals, which is a surprise. Here we go for the women’s 4x100m. Can the women match the men? Can Amy Hunt win her third gold medal of the championships? She’s already got the 100m and the 200m in the bag … “Super sweet … this team is incredible,” says Jeremiah Azu. “From the start of this year we set out these goals and we’re ticking them off …. We are in a great place.” “The body’s not been the best for about a month, I gave everything,” says Louis Hinchcliffe. “We knew once we were in the finals, we’d bring it,” says Zharnell Hughes. “I could feel the energy … “I handed off to Romell … I said to Romell, you best run bro! And he ran!” “My main aim was to get a gold medal, we accomplished that, so looking forward to the future,” says Glave. Romell Glave brings it home in 38.45sec for the home team, the favourites, and deservedly so! Zharnell Hughes looked to be celebrating when he handed the baton to Glave for the final leg. Jeremiah Azu ran the first leg, Louie Hinchliffe the second. Germany were second, Belgium third. It’s business time … the men’s 4x100 relay is here. Andreas Almgren and team are loving life after his win for Sweden in the men’s 10,000m. An incredible run it was, too. Nearly time for the men’s 4x100m relay final. Always a bit of fun. He’s broken Steve Backley’s long-standing European record with a throw of 90.40m. Nick Thumm, Weber’s teammate, had one last attempt … but it looks like he got injured on the run-up. He has a little lie-down after throwing the javelin a little way in front of him. Julian Weber of Germany lobs a javelin 90.40m! Wow! They were struggling to reach 80m and then Weber produced something ridiculous. A great bronze medal for Andrew Coscoran of Ireland, surging past Heyward at the last. Pihlström looks truly delighted with silver. “I thought I was in a perfect spot with 150m to go,” says Wightman. “Frustrating, I gave it a go, it just wasn’t there tonight. “I just popped on that home straight. It’s frustrating, it was a great opportunity in front of a home crowd there.” Wightman and Heyward were leading on the turn into the home straight … but Nillessen roared home. Pihlström (Sweden) second, Coscoran (Ireland) third. GB in fourth, fifth and sixth: Heyward, Ludewick, Wightman. Lining up for the men’s 1,500m final now. Arlo Ludewick runs for Great Britain, alongside the two Jakes, Wightman and Heyward. Morgan Lake has cleared 1.88m in the women’s high jump and is in with a shout of a medal. Coming up, the men’s 1,500m: on the card for 9.07pm UK time. It’s a time of 27min 23.44sec, a championship record. That was a phenomenal performance. “Utterly, utterly dominant,” says Cotter on the BBC. This is a slicker running performance than that of Leo Neugebauer, who collapsed over the line in the final event of the decathlon to claim gold. (It was of course a sensational all-round display.) Almgren is through 9,000m! Lobalu is clear in silver medal position. This is glory for Sweden barring disasters. Andrew Cotter helpfully explains, for anyone who’s just switched on, that the group Almgren is with have all been lapped. Almgren is lapping a massive group of rivals. chineseSummary: 英国女子和男子男子 4x100 米接力比赛均获胜，安德烈亚斯·阿尔姆格伦 (Andreas Almgren) 代表瑞典夺得男子 10,000 米接力冠军
chineseContent: 艾米·亨特在五天内赢得了令人震惊的第三枚欧洲金牌后，她就指出了那些引导她更接近历史的女超人。 “我们是神奇的四人组，”她说。很难反驳这一点，尤其是在观看了英国女子 4x100 米以 42.05 秒的成绩夺冠之后，领先瑞士和波兰 10 多米。亨特说：“能够与这些女士以及我们带来的个人超能力一起走上赛道，真是一种荣幸。” “这不是开玩笑。我们都是女超人。”肖恩·英格尔在伯明翰的报告很快就会发布。乌克兰选手雅罗斯拉瓦·马胡奇赫连续第三次获得欧洲冠军。波兰选手玛丽亚·佐齐克 (Maria Zodzik) 获得银牌，黑山选手玛丽亚·武科维奇 (Marija Vukovic) 获得铜牌。与此同时，意大利选手安迪·迪亚兹(Andy Diaz)以18.15m的成绩获得男子三级跳远。葡萄牙选手佩德罗·皮查多 (Pedro Pichardo) 以 17.76m 获得银牌，意大利选手安德里亚·达拉瓦莱 (Andrea Dallavalle) 以 17.37m 获得铜牌。通过 BBC，分析师杰西卡·恩尼斯·希尔 (Jessica Ennis Hill) 在谈到英国队的 4x100 米接力胜利时表示：“这是一个非常独特的时刻，因为我们经常遇到这样的情况：一支接力队表现出色，而另一支接力队却丢了接力棒。让他们一起庆祝对他们来说是一个独特的时刻。两枚出色的金牌。”意大利（8金4银5铜）17英国（6金5银1铜）12德国（4金7银4铜）15荷兰（4金3银5铜）12挪威（4金0银2铜）6英国男女接力队全家福。伟大的成功！ “我的工作就是让这些女士处于有利的位置，以便她们能够展示自己的卓越和才能，”阿舍-史密斯说。 “我只是想，尽可能快地跑吧！我们先把接力棒拿回家吧。” “我是圣
